title: Global cooperation is reconfiguring from broad multilateralism toward smaller coalitions, with technology and climate cooperation stronger than peace and security cooperation
source_unit: World Economic Forum and McKinsey & Company, Global Cooperation Barometer 2026, Third Edition
geography: Global cooperation across countries and economies, with indicators spanning all geographies and levels of development from 2012-2024 and partial 2025 updates

observations.period: 2012-2024; global cooperation measurement frame indexed to 2020

denominator.unit: cooperation indicators across five global-connection pillars

pillars.value: trade and capital; innovation and technology; climate and natural capital; health and wellness; peace and security

observations.method: The barometer combines action metrics showing manifested cooperation and outcome metrics influenced by cooperation plus other factors; pillar and overall indices use equal-weighted averages.
observations.uncertainty: The tool is explicitly incomplete; data availability differs by indicator and some 2025 figures are partial-year data or projections, while outcomes are not attributable to cooperation alone.
observations.subgroup: States, regional blocs, firms, research networks, civil society, multilateral institutions, and populations affected by cross-border cooperation or fragmentation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A composite index can show broad direction while masking sharp divergence within pillars, regions, income groups, and specific cooperative arrangements.

observations.period: 2019-2025; evolution of multilateral and smaller-coalition cooperation

multilateralism.value: cooperation tied to broad multilateral mechanisms has largely declined

minilateralism.value: smaller, adaptive, purpose-built coalitions have continued and become more prominent

metric_baseline.value: most cooperation metrics remain above 2019 levels

observations.method: The report interprets 41 action and outcome metrics alongside global political and economic developments to distinguish broad multilateral cooperation from flexible smaller-group cooperation.
observations.uncertainty: The reported shift is an interpretation of trends and arrangements, not a complete inventory of coalitions or proof that smaller groups are more legitimate, equitable, or durable.
observations.subgroup: National governments, regional partnerships, trade and technology coalitions, multilateral institutions, and communities affected by changing global rules.
observations.counterinterpretation: Smaller coalitions may preserve practical cooperation but can also fragment standards, exclude weaker actors, and weaken universal accountability.

innovation_climate.value: innovation and technology and climate and natural capital show increasing cooperation

trade_capital.value: trade and capital cooperation remains above 2019 levels but is flattening and reconfiguring

health.value: health and wellness cooperation is flattening, with outcomes still above pre-COVID levels but vulnerable to declining aid

peace_security.value: peace and security shows the greatest decline, with every metric below pre-pandemic levels

observations.method: The barometer compares action and outcome indices across the five pillars and identifies where domestic interests converge or conflict with global goals.
observations.uncertainty: Pillar-level patterns aggregate heterogeneous indicators and cannot establish a single cause for divergence or predict the durability of cooperation.
observations.subgroup: People exposed to conflict, health-system strain, climate risk, technology transitions, trade reconfiguration, and unequal access to cooperative gains.
observations.counterinterpretation: Strong technology or climate cooperation can coexist with conflict, exclusion, or extractive arrangements; positive aggregate momentum is not equivalent to universal benefit.

observations.period: 2019-2025; decline in multilateral security and assistance mechanisms

peacekeeping_resolutions_health_aid.value: peacekeeping activity, multilateral resolutions, and health aid were each more than 20 percent below 2019 levels by the end of 2024

foreign_aid_2024.unit: percent change in foreign aid in 2024, as reported

security_gap.value: cooperation has receded most sharply where conflict and humanitarian need are rising

observations.method: The report compares cooperation-related flows and institutional activity against 2019 pre-pandemic levels and places them alongside conflict and humanitarian trends.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison does not show whether declining activity reflects capacity, political choice, measurement coverage, or temporary shocks, and does not estimate effects on specific affected populations.
observations.subgroup: Conflict-affected communities, humanitarian recipients, peacekeeping and health institutions, aid-dependent governments, and states seeking alternative security partnerships.
observations.counterinterpretation: Declines in broad multilateral measures may coexist with bilateral, regional, or informal cooperation that the selected indicators do not capture.

related_sources.claim: Full report, executive summary, recommendations, and appendix navigation.
Recommendations for adaptive and interest-aligned forms of cooperation.

boundary: This record adds a global-cooperation and institutional-reconfiguration route linking trade, technology, climate, health, peace, multilateralism, minilateralism, and uneven geopolitical consequences. It is a composite index and expert/executive survey-informed synthesis, not a causal measure of cooperation, a complete coalition inventory, respondent-level public opinion, or proof that smaller coalitions produce equitable outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official WEF Global Cooperation Barometer 2026 pages were reviewed for the five pillars, 41 indicators, 2012-2024 frame, 2020 index base, steady overall cooperation, multilateral decline and minilateral adaptation, pillar divergence, and pre-pandemic security and aid comparisons.
